findings.summary: Zero-award grants attempt to write an invalid ledger entry
findings.details: When budget/user/partner caps reduce awarded to zero, grantReward still saves the reward transaction and unconditionally calls walletService.creditInCurrentTx(..., awarded, ...). That path writes a ledger_entries.amount value with the same amount, but the new ledger schema requires amount > 0. A fully exhausted cap therefore turns an expected capped/no-award outcome into a database constraint failure and rolls back the whole grant path.
findings.recommendation: Skip wallet credit and ledger creation when awarded.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) == 0; add integration test against real ledger constraint for exhausted-budget grants.

findings.summary: Partner caps can be overrun by concurrent grants to different users
findings.details: The advisory lock serializes only incentiveId:userId, but the partner-cap calculation sums all awards for partnerCompanyId. Two users from the same partner can run concurrently under different lock keys, both read the same partner total, and both award against the same remaining cap before either transaction commits.
findings.recommendation: Use lock key incentiveId:partnerCompanyId when checking partner caps, or lock a durable partner-cap utilization row before reading/updating the total.

findings.summary: Settlement can be skipped after reserve when the same redemption reference is reused
findings.details: doDebitInTx treats any ledger row with the same wallet/reference pair as a duplicate, without checking entry_type. A reserve+debit lifecycle using the same referenceType will cause the debit to see the RESERVE row and return without reducing reserved balance or writing a DEBIT row.
findings.recommendation: Scope idempotency checks by entry_type plus wallet/reference, or use operation-specific referenceType constants consistently; add lifecycle test that reserves and debits with the same redemption reference id.

classificationRules.blockingThreshold: severity critical/high AND confidence >= 0.70 AND not alreadyHandled
classificationRules.advisoryThreshold: severity medium/low OR confidence < 0.70 OR alreadyHandled
